newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Siemens Nixdorf wants double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Siemens Nixdorf wants double-digit growth.

text.p: Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG, the Siemens AG computer unit, said on Thursday it had set a goal of at least 10 percent growth in 1996/97 -- the target it failed to reach in 1995/96.

"We must as a company learn to achieve double-digit growth," chief executive Gerhard Schulmeyer told a news conference. "If we don't, we would have to restructure again. With minor growth, we don't have the productivity levels we need to compete in this business."

Siemens Nixdorf on Wednesday reported 29 million marks ($19.35 million) in net profit for the 1995/96 business year, up 26 percent from 1994/95. Last week, parent Siemens said the computer company's sales grew six percent to 13.6 billion marks, while pre-tax profit fell 19 percent to 52 million.
Schulmeyer said pre-tax profits were hurt by a 51 million mark write-off related to Siemens Nixdorf's stake in Escom, a computer retailer that went bankrupt in July.

The sale of its high-end printer business in April also lowered its second-half results in 1995-96, he said. "Without these two situations, pre-tax profit could have been 133 million," Schulmeyer said.

Even with these costs behind it, Siemens Nixdorf will have difficulty surpassing 10 percent growth in the year which will end on September 30 unless it gets a boost from the Germany economy, analysts said.
In 1995/96, 63 percent of the company's sales -- 8.5 billion marks -- came from Germany, where Siemens Nixdorf's revenues only grew two percent.
"This dependence on Germany and Europe must be reduced," said Hans Peter Wodniok of Credit Lyonnais in Frankfurt. "That is the question: Can they do that?"
"They have been trying to do that for years, since the '80s, and it's harder to do now because competitors have already established strong holds on the market," he said.
The rest of Europe generated 30 percent of Siemens Nixdorf's 1995-96 sales, and the rest of the world seven percent. Sales outside of Germany grew 13 percent to 5.1 billion marks.
Wodniok forecast Siemens Nixdorf will see profit rise slightly, with net income level or lower net income.
Siemens Nixdorf is counting on growth from a new Internet services group and a jump in PC sales, Schulmeyer said.

Formed recently by merging the Siemens Nixdorf computer services business with Siemens' Networking Systems Group, the IT Networks business unit will help customers build sites on the Internet, Schulmeyer said. The unit begins with 600 employees and 500 million marks in business volume.

To boost PC results, the company is looking to expand indirect sales through resellers and stores, especially in other countries, Schulmeyer said. "We want to move out of Europe, rather than grow within Europe," he said.
Schulmeyer also said the company must continue to reduce costs and raise productivity, although he ruled out shifting operations out of German's high-cost labour market.
"Things would only happen if we really came into a problem," he said. Parent Siemens' labor costs rose seven percent in the past year, he added.

Siemens Nixdorf increased productivity nine percent in 1995-96, lowering the payroll nine percent to 34,100 workers. Part of the productivity rise stemmed from a massive reorganisation that created more than 250 profit centres, each responsible for separate product lines in different countries.
